To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Nurses need to develop their information literacy skills in order to be able to access, evaluate and use information in a way that is consistent with their own values and beliefs” (Duncan, 2007, p. 1).
the nurses in our study reported that they had difficulty in finding and evaluating the information needed for evidence-based nursing practice.

the nurses’ knowledge acquisition and information literacy skills can be enhanced through the development of a new model for information literacy that includes the individual nature of knowledge acquisition and information seeking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how nurses can acquire and apply information literacy skills to improve their practice.
the acquisition of knowledge and the development of information literacy in the context of nursing practice.
the nature and extent of knowledge acquisition and the information literacy of nursing professionals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nurses need to be able to access, evaluate, and use information in order to provide quality patient care and that the acquisition of this knowledge is not an easy task.
nurses are not only responsible for acquiring knowledge, but also responsible for acquiring knowledge about knowledge acquisition.
the acquisition and development of information literacy skills are essential in nursing practice, but are not always acquired or developed to a satisfactory degree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge acquisition and the development of information literacy in nursing education is not a linear process.
knowledge acquisition is a process of personal and professional development that requires an individual’s commitment to lifelong learning and a commitment to the profession.

the acquisition of advanced information literacy skills is not only about the individual learner but also about how the learner is able to acquire knowledge that is useful for the practice of nursing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nurses are not only information users; they are also information creators.
information literacy skills are essential to the development of nursing knowledge.
nurses need to develop the ability to identify and understand the knowledge and information they need, and to be able to access it, in order to provide safe, effective care.
